subtitle: Spain, France, and England sit atop the 2026 FIFA World Cup winner market as the leading European contenders, with implied probabilities clustered tightly between 11% and 17% amid strong recent form and squad depth. Spain’s status as the most recent European champions, combined with an unbeaten run in competitive matches stretching back over two years, underpins its narrow edge, though Lamine Yamal’s April hamstring injury introduced minor uncertainty around attacking options. France benefits from its 2022 final appearance, consistent qualification results, and proven knockout experience under Didier Deschamps, while England’s back-to-back European Championship final runs highlight sustained progress despite a recent dip in friendlies. The expanded 48-team field and one-month lead-in to the June 11 opener in North America leave room for momentum shifts from injuries or group-stage results, keeping the race among these sides and Brazil, Argentina, and Portugal highly competitive.
